subtitle: Connect local Hmong and Hmong American context with each person’s own meaning, useful communication and respectful participation. This helps you work with Hmong communities with more care.
scope: For staff across DHS working with Hmong and Hmong American Minnesotans. Original practice adults explain individually learned meanings; none represents a generation, language variety, clan, gender or faith. Local cultural resources invite further learning, not a prediction of immigration history, literacy, authority or service eligibility. Actual language access, information permissions, decision and reporting responsibilities continue through their applicable processes. Learning is voluntary. Private reflection with the full example is valid; no live case, family history or cultural disclosure is required. Native American and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: Learn from local Hmong cultural resources while keeping the actual person and question visible. Compare two individually meanings the people describe of when to ask a question, follow Pao’s communication request and preserve chosen participation, real responsibilities and unanswered outcomes. You can develop a wider understanding privately using the full example. Learn at your own pace.

lessons.summary: Learn from Hmong Minnesota resources while preserving the actual person’s present question.

objectives: Distinguish a local historical resource from a prediction about Pao.
Identify the information Pao actually wants to understand.

takeaways: Historical and cultural resources can widen understanding.
An identity does not establish the person’s current needs.
The present question deserves an accurate response.
lessons.statement: Use context to notice more without deciding who the person must be.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: Pao asks about information, not a profile
intro.body:
Respectful work with Hmong communities can begin with local history and living cultural resources. Minnesota Historical Society resources describe Hmong arrival in Minnesota beginning in 1975 and document arts, stories and community contributions. The Hmong Cultural Center describes educational, arts and library work. These resources offer ways to learn beyond a narrow service encounter without turning the person involved into a required cultural teacher.

Keep the role of that context clear. A historical arrival account does not establish that every Hmong Minnesotan came through the same route or has the same language, faith or family practice. An institution’s arts program does not show what a particular person values. The course uses a brief local introduction, not a current population estimate or a clinical, immigration or literacy profile.

In the example, Pao identifies as a Hmong Minnesotan and asks about the purpose of a notice in a covered health-program activity. Pao wants to discuss particular terms in a usable spoken form. Staff member Victor initially assumes that Pao’s age means a relative should explain everything. The example describes no such preferred decision arrangement or assessment of Pao’s ability.

A useful first response receives Pao’s actual notice question and asks what communication route is needed through the applicable process. Victor can explain what is confirmed and who can arrange an appropriate response. Pao does not need to describe a migration history, family role or cultural tradition before the question is addressed. Actual program information requirements remain separate and should be explained accurately.

The photograph also has a limited role. It shows people sitting with work materials, not their ethnicity, language, faith or medical status. No Hmong identity is inferred from their appearance. An engaging image can accompany learning without becoming evidence about the person or a community.

Privately separate the source’s local context from Victor’s added story and Pao’s actual request. You may recognize a habit of letting age and identity supply an answer before hearing the person. The full example provides enough material to reconsider that interpretation and prepare a useful question. No real notice, cultural interview or live service contact is required for learning.

lessons.keyStatement: A historical resource and a present communication request answer different questions.

lessons.title: Understand different meanings of question timing
lessons.summary: Compare two individually learned meanings of respectful listening and early inquiry, then widen the invitation.
lessons.objective: Explain Ntxawm’s and Mai’s meanings the people describe of when to ask a question.
objectives: Explain Ntxawm’s and Mai’s meanings the people describe of when to ask a question.
Distinguish quiet listening from assumed agreement and early questions from assumed disrespect.
Develop an invitation that preserves contribution without ranking generations.
takeaways: Question timing can carry a learned meaning.
Quiet and early questions do not establish agreement or disrespect by themselves.
An invitation can adapt while preserving the actual information and purpose.
lessons.statement: Understand what the timing means before treating it as agreement or disrespect.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: Two individually meanings the people describe widen Victor’s view
intro.body:
When a person asks a question can have a meaning beyond the words of the question. Staff may read silence as agreement or an early interruption as disregard for the speaker. Those interpretations need the actual context. A Hmong identity or an age difference does not supply a single rule for respectful communication.

In the example, Ntxawm and Mai join an optional discussion about an information explanation. Ntxawm describes an earlier family sewing circle in which listening to the complete story before asking a question showed care for the person whose experience was being shared. Ntxawm wants time to receive the whole account before identifying a concern. Silence during the first passage is not an endorsement of every detail.

Mai describes a Hmong American student newspaper group in which asking a question while an article was being developed expressed care for the story and its subjects. An early question could prevent an inaccurate statement from becoming the public account. Mai wants to ask about a term as it appears, not dismiss the speaker’s contribution. These are original individually supplied experiences, not findings about generations or Hmong family norms.

Victor initially treats Ntxawm’s quiet listening as agreement and Mai’s early question as impatience. After hearing both explanations, Victor can reconsider the meaning of the behavior. A wider invitation may explain that questions can be noted during the account, asked at an appropriate point or received after the whole account through a stated route. Participants can choose how to contribute within the actual discussion purpose.

The invitation still needs accurate information and usable participation. Offering different question routes does not turn an unconfirmed service description into a fact or authorize a new procedure. Victor should explain the actual limits and ask whether the invitation supports the stated purpose. Both people may revise what helps in a different setting or decline to share any further history.

The Council of Europe source explains contextual, personalized meanings and the possibility of learning about one’s own assumptions through another perspective. Privately examine Victor’s first reading and the changed invitation. Understanding the supplied timing meanings can be intrinsically useful without assigning an IDI stage, ranking age groups or requiring a live meeting. The full example is enough for reflection and practice.

inThisLesson: A wider invitation and actual limits.
lessons.keyStatement: A behavior can be visible while its personally learned meaning remains different from the first interpretation.

items.title: Quiet does not settle agreement
items.body: Ntxawm describes listening before identifying a concern. Victor cannot treat the first quiet passage as consent to every detail. A stated later question route can receive that contribution without forcing immediate speech to prove engagement.

items.title: An early question can express care
items.body: Mai connects the timing to protecting accuracy in the earlier newspaper group. This widens Victor’s reading of an interruption. It does not make every early question automatically appropriate; the actual purpose and interaction still matter.

items.title: Adapt without a generational ranking
items.body: Victor can offer ways to hold and ask questions while keeping the same explanation and actual limits visible. Neither method is a higher cultural stage. The changed response follows individually meanings the people describe rather than an assumption about older or younger Hmong people.

tabs.label: Quiet means agreement
tabs.body: Victor concludes that Ntxawm endorses the explanation before hearing the later concern. This makes the staff interpretation larger than the observed behavior. Receive the actual account and provide a useful route for questions rather than use silence as proof.

tabs.label: Early means disrespect
tabs.body: Victor dismisses Mai’s question as impatience. That overlooks its stated accuracy purpose and could leave a term unexplored. Understanding the purpose supports an appropriate response without removing every practical limit on a discussion.

tabs.label: Different meanings, useful question routes
tabs.body: Victor explains how participants can note, ask or share questions within the discussion’s actual purpose. Ntxawm and Mai retain their contribution without a rank. The invitation can be examined for fit rather than declared universally effective.

lessons.title: Receive the specific communication need
lessons.summary: Distinguish language variety, written information and spoken explanation without inferring ability from an identity or a document label.
lessons.objective: Identify Pao’s actual spoken communication request.
objectives: Identify Pao’s actual spoken communication request.

lessons.statement: Keep language, content and the person’s task connected.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: The notice terms need a usable discussion
intro.body:
A person’s communication need can be more specific than a general document label. The written form, spoken language variety, relevant terms and opportunity to ask can all matter to the actual task. Staff should receive the person’s account and use the relevant assistance process rather than predict literacy or ability from identity, age or an accent.

In the example, Pao asks to discuss the notice terms in White Hmong. A written item labeled Hmong has been offered, but Pao says that it does not settle the particular spoken explanation needed. The case does not establish that Pao cannot read, that every Hmong reader needs the same form or that the offered document is inaccurate. It establishes a specific remaining communication question.

The Minnesota Historical Society’s exhibit offers distinct Green and White Hmong audio presentations alongside written material. That illustrates why a single broad language label should not replace a particular inquiry. The exhibit is a cultural presentation, not a clinical interpreting standard. Its description of natural oral expression does not authorize staff to omit important notice content or substitute unverified paraphrase in a service encounter.

For the practice covered health-program activity, current 45 CFR 92.201 requires appropriate qualified interpretation or translation when required under its scope, with accurate, timely, free language assistance that protects privacy and independent decision making. The actual process should identify the needed communication and relevant qualifications. Being bilingual or choosing a familiar language variety does not by itself establish every interpreting or translation qualification.

Victor can receive Pao’s actual request, explain the available assistance route and confirm what remains to be arranged. If Pao cannot ask the particular notice question through an offered route, the task is not established as resolved merely because a document was delivered. The source regulation also does not compel acceptance of offered assistance. An appropriate response preserves the person’s choice and actual requirements rather than turn an offer into a forced arrangement.

Privately identify what is known and what remains open. Pao has supplied the desired spoken form and terms to discuss, while the actual arrangement and its usefulness still need confirmation. No live interpretation, medical history or literacy test is required to complete this learning. Actual current needs still require their responsible response; the course is not a reason to postpone them.

items.title: Ask rather than diagnose
items.body: Pao’s spoken request does not establish inability to read or understand. It identifies what is useful for this explanation. A task-focused question can preserve that purpose without an age-based judgment or a classroom literacy test.

items.title: Keep source roles distinct
items.body: The exhibit’s language presentations show cultural variation in a public learning resource. They are not permission to change rights, notice meaning or health-program information. Accurate service communication needs its actual standards and qualified roles.

items.title: Confirm usefulness without forcing acceptance
items.body: An assistance offer and a resolved question are different states. Receive the actual task feedback and use the relevant process for an unresolved need. The federal rule does not require the person to accept an offered service, and declining one option is not proof that all communication needs are met.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: A niece can help hold questions without deciding the task
intro.body:
Chosen support can be meaningful without replacing the person’s own direction. Staff should clarify what help the person wants and keep that distinct from qualifications, representative roles and information permissions. A family relationship is not a complete legal or communication account. A Hmong identity does not establish that a particular relative must make decisions.

In the example, Pao brings a willing adult niece, Mee, to help keep a list of questions. Pao says that Mee should help hold the questions but that Pao wants the explanation and relevant decision discussion directed personally. Mee agrees to that limited support. The example describes neither an interpreting qualification nor authorization for unrestricted record access or a substitute decision.

Victor initially assumes that the niece should interpret and make the choice because that seems like culturally respectful family involvement. Pao’s supplied purpose is different. A more respectful response asks how the question-list support should be used, preserves Pao’s own communication and uses the applicable qualified language-assistance route. Respect is expressed through the actual chosen arrangement, not the staff member’s community rule.

Within covered health-program communication, current 45 CFR 92.201 restricts reliance on an accompanying adult who is not qualified as an interpreter. Its narrow nonemergency requested-adult exception requires specific private request safeguards, the adult’s agreement, documentation and appropriateness; a person simply arriving with a relative is not enough. The course does not adjudicate an exception or approve a medical disclosure. Staff should use the actual responsible process and applicable guidance.

Mee’s question support can be considered with Pao’s choice and the real information-handling requirements. If a matter requires a different authorized role, explain that distinction rather than silently enlarge the niece’s task. Pao may decline a family-history question or change what help is wanted. Staff learning does not require disclosure of clan, migration, faith or family decision practices.

Privately examine Victor’s first interpretation and the response that follows Pao’s supplied preference. You can understand the difference between respecting support and assigning authority without a live family encounter. Actual process requirements still apply; the learning should not erase them or promise that every chosen arrangement is automatically permitted. The useful insight is that care and personal direction can be considered together through the actual person’s account.

items.title: Keep the question-list purpose
items.body: Mee helps retain questions while Pao receives the explanation and direction remains personal. Treating Mee as decision maker would change the supplied arrangement. Clarify what help is chosen rather than expand it from the family relationship.

items.title: Use the actual interpreting process
items.body: An accompanying adult does not automatically meet qualification or restricted-use conditions. The nonemergency requested-adult exception has specific private request and documentation safeguards, not a general family preference rule. Use responsible guidance rather than improvise an approval from the lesson.

items.title: Respect an optional history boundary
items.body: Pao need not explain a family tradition for the stated help to be considered. Any actual permission or process information has its own role and should be explained accurately. Cultural disclosure should not become a condition of receiving the practical response.

tabs.label: Family means all authority
tabs.body: Victor assigns interpretation, decision and record access to Mee from the relationship. That exceeds the supplied question-list purpose and the case’s permissions. Cultural respect cannot substitute for actual role requirements or Pao’s direction.

tabs.label: Independence means no chosen help
tabs.body: Victor excludes Mee to prove that Pao can decide alone. This removes the supplied support preference without considering its purpose. A willing person can help retain questions while actual qualifications, permissions and personal direction remain distinct.

tabs.label: Chosen help and clear roles
tabs.body: Victor receives the limited support purpose and uses the actual communication and information process. The explanation remains directed to Pao. Other roles require their relevant basis rather than arise automatically from identity, age or relationship.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: A question about timing is useful without being a community verdict
intro.body:
A respectful participation approach can produce useful information without establishing a complete community view. Keep each contribution connected to its source, purpose and limits. A cultural resource, a service question and a formal program decision are related but different parts of the work. Treating one as proof of all the others weakens the account rather than strengthens it.

In the example, Victor prepares a proposed service explanation for the person responsible in the program. Ntxawm identifies a way to hear the whole account before asking a question. Mai identifies a critical term that could be clarified earlier. Each explains a particular practical contribution; neither says that all Hmong Minnesotans want the same approach or endorses the entire proposed explanation.

Victor can carry both contributions into the review. One option is to make room for questions at appropriate points and after the account while preserving accurate content and actual communication arrangements. Whether that proposal fits the real service requirements belongs to the relevant responsible process. No immediate publication authority, eligibility finding or completed formal equity analysis is supplied by the practice conversation.

Local institutions also have a specific role. An arts, educational or library resource can widen staff learning and help identify questions worth pursuing. It is not automatically the place to check the service explanation for technical accuracy. Staff should not claim an institution supported a proposal because its resource was used, or require a person to obtain a cultural organization’s approval before a current communication need is addressed.

A separate employment concern requires its own response. In the example, Hmong American employee Bao tells manager Cora that national-origin comments accompanied exclusion from an assignment. Under MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow actual procedures. Cora cannot postpone that responsibility for a listening event, ask Bao to prove a community pattern first, or put the allegation in public course materials. Actual assigned investigation and corrective-action responsibilities remain under the applicable procedures.

The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads this program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback; staff develop and carry out their own equity work within their roles. The optional course does not complete every requirement of DHS Equity Policy or approve a program change. Privately separate the contributions, the proposed response and the responsible next steps. That distinction is useful even when you use only the full example and share nothing about a real case.

lessons.keyStatement: A useful contribution does not replace the appropriate decision, analysis or reporting process.

accordion.heading: Carry input into the right work

items.title: Keep both contributions useful
items.body: Ntxawm’s full-account question route and Mai’s early clarification can inform a proposal without deciding that one person is more culturally correct. Name how each idea affects the proposed explanation. If the person responsible retains an existing choice, explain the relevant reason rather than claim that participation failed unless every suggestion was adopted.

items.title: Distinguish resource and approval
items.body: A cultural center’s library can deepen understanding of local history, but that does not establish expertise or authority over a particular health-program notice. Treat the source as a learning resource unless an actual review role is established. The relevant program owner still needs an accurate explanation and a usable communication arrangement.

items.title: Keep reporting immediate
items.body: Cora has received a protected-class allegation in a manager role. Optional learning or a broader participation plan cannot delay the immediate HR or agency Affirmative Action Officer report. Follow actual procedures and assigned responsibilities without deciding the allegation is established or requiring Bao to recruit corroborating community accounts first.

tabs.label: One account becomes everyone’s preference
tabs.body: Victor labels Ntxawm’s contribution the Hmong community’s choice. That removes Mai’s distinct contribution and attributes agreement to people who have not provided it. The resulting proposal has less accurate evidence even if it sounds confident.

tabs.label: Every contribution automatically changes the notice
tabs.body: Victor immediately posts every suggested wording change without the responsible review. Participation can reveal useful options, but it does not establish content accuracy, authority or complete access. Explain the proposed change and its evidence through the relevant process.

tabs.label: Specific input informs an accountable proposal
tabs.body: Victor keeps the two contributions attributed and explains their possible effects on question timing and term clarity. The person responsible considers actual content and access requirements. This supports practical action without claiming a community verdict or a completed formal analysis.

check.feedbackIncorrect: Waiting for learning delays the manager’s reporting duty. A community-pattern demand adds an unsupported gate to reporting the supplied allegation. Public use of the allegation is not an appropriate substitute for the actual employment process.

Mai identifies a term needing earlier clarification.
The person responsible in the program considers the proposed explanation.
Cora immediately reports the protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer.
An arts resource automatically approves the health-program notice.
One participant’s idea represents every Hmong Minnesotan.

lessons.next: Review the specific response without turning missing outcomes into approval.

scenario.context: Ntxawm and Mai supplied different useful contributions. Victor has a proposal, not a publication approval or a complete community view.
options: Both contributions automatically approve immediate publication.
Keep the attributed contributions and proposed effects for the responsible review without a community agreement claim.
Discard both unless every Hmong participant agrees.
responses: No such publication authority is supplied.
This retains useful input and the relevant responsibilities.
Unanimous cultural agreement is not established as a gate to considering the contributions.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain one contribution, its proposed effect and the actual responsibility that still applies.

move.control: You can connect the contribution to a proposed response within your role.
move.failure: Input becomes universal endorsement or an excuse to delay a separate duty.
move.next: If useful, use the full example to prepare the account. No actual allegation, community interview or publication is required.

lessons.title: Review the specific response without a community verdict
lessons.summary: Recognize a changed interpretation and retain the task outcomes that are still unknown.
lessons.objective: Describe how the meanings the people describe informed Victor’s changed response.
objectives: Describe how the meanings the people describe informed Victor’s changed response.
Distinguish the observed question experience from unconfirmed service outcomes.
Choose a follow-up account that preserves disagreement, private learning and actual responsibilities.
takeaways: A particular changed response can be described accurately.
Private understanding has value without a universal success claim.
lessons.statement: Name what changed, who supplied the feedback and what you still do not know.

image.caption: People sit around a table with laptops, notebooks and papers; one person gestures with open hands.

intro.heading: A wider response can matter without proving the whole service works
intro.body:
Follow-through should preserve the same care for meaning and evidence used at the start. A changed invitation or question route can be described without declaring every need met. Keep the supplied response, the person’s feedback and the unconfirmed outcomes distinct. This avoids turning a satisfying learning moment into an unsupported service claim.

In the final fiction, Victor receives Ntxawm’s question after the full account instead of interpreting quiet listening as agreement. Mai asks an earlier question about a critical term. Victor can explain why those different approaches may express care for understanding rather than infer reluctance from one and impatience from the other. The wider interpretation supports a more useful response without diagnosing either person’s intercultural orientation.

Ntxawm says that the later question opportunity helped retain the intended point. Mai says that the earlier exchange clarified one term while another wording question remains. These are distinct attributed accounts. They do not establish unanimous approval, improved eligibility decisions, a complete community consultation or a lasting effect across all service encounters. Mai’s unresolved wording is part of the evidence, not resistance that should be removed from the account.

Pao’s covered health-program communication need still has its actual route. The final fiction does not supply a completed qualified-assistance arrangement or a confirmed notice outcome for Pao. Mee’s willingness to retain questions does not fill those gaps. Do not label the service accessible, the notice understood or the person satisfied merely because the learning conversation went well. Appropriate current access and information responsibilities remain active.

Victor may next explain the remaining term question to the person responsible and accurately describe any confirmed communication arrangement. The course does not authorize a particular release, assign a new deadline or decide the employment allegation. Cora’s Policy 1436 responsibility remains separate and immediate, with actual procedures and assigned roles preserved. If no additional feedback is supplied, it stays missing; silence is not proof of consent, refusal, motive or a successful outcome.

Private learning can also be a meaningful result. You might notice that your own understanding of respectful questioning had been narrower than the two individually meanings the people describe. That insight does not require a live case, a recorded work product, a cultural interview or personal disclosure. Use the example to name the interpretation reconsidered, the response it changes and the questions still open. The value lies in more accurate understanding and practical judgment, not a rank, a compulsory output or a prediction about Hmong communities.

lessons.keyStatement: A changed interpretation, a participant account and a service outcome need separate evidence.

flashcards.back: Victor no longer treats quiet as agreement or an early question as impatience.
The particular response Ntxawm or Mai supplied.
Pao’s qualified-assistance arrangement and notice result are not supplied.
A meaningful personal insight that need not be disclosed or assessed.

items.title: Explain the change precisely
items.body: Victor’s receiving approach follows the individually meanings the people describe rather than a profile of age, generation or identity. Describe that particular response. Do not claim that one brief practice proves an intercultural orientation or makes every future encounter effective.

items.title: Keep Mai’s remaining question
items.body: One term became clearer while another wording issue remains. Retaining both parts of Mai’s account identifies where the next review may help. Removing the unresolved question would create a more reassuring report but a less accurate basis for action.

items.title: Keep the actual service outcome open
items.body: The story does not establish Pao’s completed qualified-assistance arrangement. Mee’s presence and the other participants’ feedback answer different questions. Name the missing confirmation and use the appropriate actual route rather than infer access from the course’s positive interaction.

tabs.label: The conversation proves complete access
tabs.body: Victor claims every Hmong user can now understand the notice because the learning exchange felt productive. That extends two participant accounts to unknown people and unconfirmed tasks. It also hides Pao’s actual pending communication need.

tabs.label: One remaining question means no learning occurred
tabs.body: Victor dismisses the wider receiving approach because Mai still questions wording. Learning and an unresolved content issue can coexist. Her account supplies a useful next question without erasing Ntxawm’s specific experience or Victor’s changed interpretation.

tabs.label: Specific progress and remaining needs
tabs.body: Victor describes the changed response, attributes both accounts and identifies what is unconfirmed for Pao. The person responsible can consider the remaining term question. Actual service and reporting routes continue, while private learning remains meaningful in its own right.

check.question: Which final account fits the supplied evidence?
check.correct: Victor changed the receiving approach; Ntxawm and Mai supplied distinct feedback, and Pao’s completed communication outcome remains unconfirmed.
wrong: The course proves complete access and community agreement.
Mai’s remaining question proves the changed approach failed.
No additional feedback proves that the remaining needs disappeared.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps the actual change and each account without filling the service gaps by inference.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Complete access and community agreement require evidence not supplied here. Mai’s remaining wording question does not erase the described changed response. Missing additional feedback establishes neither disappearance of needs nor consent or motive; the appropriate routes remain.

items.text: Victor receives a later question without treating quiet as agreement.
Mai says one term became clearer while another question remains.
Pao’s completed qualified-assistance arrangement is not supplied.
Other people’s notice experiences are not provided.
Every Hmong user now approves the notice.
No further feedback proves every need disappeared.

lessons.next: Use local resources and individual explanations to continue learning at your own pace.

scenario.context: The supplied final accounts describe a changed question route and mixed wording feedback. Pao’s actual communication outcome is not provided.
options: Announce universal success from the positive interaction.
Remove Mai’s unresolved question to keep the report encouraging.
Retain the specific accounts and open service question for the actual responsible process.
responses: The evidence does not support universal success.
Removing the question weakens the account and the next decision.
This preserves useful progress, uncertainty and actual responsibilities.

lessons.transfer: Privately name one interpretation reconsidered, the response it changes and one outcome still unknown.

move.control: You can describe learning and supplied feedback accurately without a ranking or disclosure.
move.failure: The account treats silence as success or discards uncertainty to sound complete.
move.next: If useful, keep a private reflection with the full example. No live case, public proof or personal cultural account is required.

jobAid.title: Make room for the person’s meaning and question
jobAid.subtitle: Use local learning, actual communication needs and appropriate roles without a cultural prediction.
jobAid.intro: Use the example privately or an appropriate question within your actual role. A personal story is not required.

sections.heading: Use local context accurately
items: MNHS and community cultural resources provide ways to learn about Hmong Minnesota; they do not establish every person’s history, faith, language or preference.
Ask what the actual person wants to understand or contribute. Do not infer literacy or ability from language choice or age.
The photo does not establish Hmong identity. No participant must represent a generation, family or community.

sections.heading: Understand meanings and communication
items: Ntxawm’s chosen full-account listening and Mai’s early-question practice express individually meanings the people describe of respect; neither is a universal Hmong rule.
Offer useful ways to ask and respond while retaining the same accurate information and actual requirements.
Receive the actual spoken or written communication need. A general translated label does not establish the right language variety, format or task understanding.

sections.heading: Keep actual roles and duties clear
items: Use qualified language assistance and the relevant process in covered health programs. A companion’s presence does not automatically establish interpreter or decision authority.
Explain any proposed arrangement and confirmation status honestly. The course cannot approve a service, eligibility, disclosure or a representative’s role.

Managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow actual procedures; optional learning cannot delay reporting.
Staff do their own equity work with guidance, knowledge and feedback from the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant, who leads the program. Actual analysis and decision responsibilities remain.

sections.heading: Review proportionately
items: Name the particular meaning reconsidered and changed response without an assessment score.
Retain attributed feedback and disagreement. Silence does not establish consent, satisfaction, refusal or motive.
Other task outcomes remain open unless actually supplied. Current needs still have their appropriate routes.
Private reflection with the example is meaningful; no live work product or disclosure is required.

remember: Local learning opens questions rather than predicts a person.
Quiet listening and early questions can have different meanings.
Language variety, written form and interpreting role are practical questions.
Chosen help does not erase personal direction or actual authority.
Learning is voluntary; required-training credit needs an expressly approved exception.
Native American and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
